snippet.title: Zoo Keeper (DS) Playthrough - NintendoComplete
snippet.description:
A playthrough of Ignition Entertainment's 2005 puzzle game for the Nintendo DS, Zoo Keeper.

This video shows two different game modes: I begin with finishing all ten stages of Quest mode. Then, at 9:57 I play the Zoo Keeper mode until it ends at level twenty. Both are played on the default difficulty level.

*I recommend watching this video on the phone app in portrait mode.*

I remember buying this as a full-price game when it first came out, and while I could easily imagine many people balking at spending $40 on such a simple game, I never once regretted it.

Like most systems, the DS's library was pretty sparse early on, and I was looking for something fun that I hadn't played yet when Zoo Keeper caught my eye. I had no idea what it was, but the box made it seem like any other Match 3 style puzzle game, so I figured I'd give it a go.

It doesn't impress with its simplistic Flash-style illustrations and animations, the insanely repetitve (and insanely catchy) background music, or its (albeit responsive and useful) touch-based control scheme, but it doesn't need to. The gameplay more than has the goods to carry the entire package.  

Very little changes over the course of a game - quotas slowly reach higher as you go up in levels and the timer begins to drain faster and faster the further you get, but the gameplay is tuned extremely well. I hope you have sharp eyes, though - you aren't given enough time to just sit there scanning the screen over and over for matches.

The Zoo Keeper mode was always my go-to gametype. Quest mode can be fun, but whether or not you win is a bit too much reliant on luck, and there isnt much reward for winning.

Even if not for the game play, what makes the Zoo Keeper mode really noteworthy is the storyline. There isnt much of one until the ending, but wow! I never expected it to have an ending, let alone the hilariously dark and melodramatic cutscene you see upon finishing the twentieth stage. It has to be one of my all-time favorite endings - I kid you not. Even if you dont watch the gameplay, do yourself a favor and watch the end. If you're anything like me, you won't know whether to crack up or to just stare with your mouth open in bewilderment.

If you like classic, simple puzzle games, they don't get much more classic or simple than Zoo Keeper. It can easily keep you entertained for days.

-Does that soundtrack remind anyone else of the music in.  Napoleon Dynamite?
_
No cheats were used during the recording of this video.
